name: Conceptual Physics Notes Course Profile
role: Current Physics-specific Notes contract. It preserves the established Notes HTML/CSS shell while using substantially more source-grounded reading and meaningful visual narrative. This profile supersedes older embedded Framework summary language that required Stop and Discuss after every substantial reading segment.

bank_canonical.rule: Finalized Unit Bank owns canonical WTC / Notes Example / Notes YTI wording, values, figures, and solutions.
bank_canonical.pair_rule: Use the Physics Bank-v2 profile: no more than four canonical Example/YTI pairs per section; Notes consumes every canonical pair actually present.
bank_canonical.display_numbering_rule: Bank IDs/pair IDs remain hidden provenance. Visible Example/You Try It numbering is assigned from final display order within the section and runs 1, 2, 3... even when Bank pair_number differs.

source_spine.rule: The Framework-declared Physics textbook is the instructional spine. Notes keep selected textbook explanation in its source order. The normal editorial operation is KEEP, CUT, or LIGHTLY PARAPHRASE/CONDENSE; do not invent a replacement close-reading passage when usable source text exists.
source_spine.close_reading_rule: Close reading means students read the retained/adapted textbook material. A single close-reading directions box appears once after the skim and before the first retained reading chunk.

architecture: Section title + exact Learning Target / I-can statements
Let's Get Started skim: headings/figures + 1-2 notices and 1-2 wonders
substantial retained/adapted textbook reading and visual flow
interleaved processing with at most one primary student-processing event per reading boundary
canonical Example / You Try It anchors, with any leftover intact pairs after the final reading
Vocabulary with definitions immediately before Summary
Framework-defined final miscellaneous workspace when required

opening.skim_prompt: Skim before close reading. Look at the headings and figures. Find 1–2 things you notice and 1–2 things you wonder about.
opening.prediction_rule: Do not add a prediction prompt unless the current Framework explicitly requires it.

reading.benchmark: Framework-declared Physics textbook / approved source spine, supported by Conceptual Physics/Hewitt visual/reference resources
reading.rule: Physics Notes are textbook-like instructional reading, not thin blurbs between problems. Preserve useful source explanation and conceptual order; cut by omission first and paraphrase only as needed for classroom clarity/length.
reading.paragraphs: multiple short developed paragraphs; avoid walls of text and one-sentence stacking

processing_rhythm.hard_rule: At a reading boundary, use at most ONE primary student-processing event: Stop and Discuss OR one canonical Example/YTI pair OR none. Do not stack Stop and Discuss and Example/YTI after the same reading chunk.
processing_rhythm.instructional_insertions: Physics Notes, diagrams, graphs, models, and other explanatory reference blocks may be embedded with the reading when they teach the idea; they are not a second required student-processing event.
processing_rhythm.leftover_pair_rule: If canonical Example/YTI pairs remain after all natural reading insertion points are used, place the remaining intact pairs after the final reading chunk in display order.

visual_storytelling.hard_rule: Use strong existing source/toolkit/Bank representations when they advance the conceptual story. Purpose-author a new Notes-specific representation only when the current map requires a need not already satisfied canonically.
visual_storytelling.not_decoration: A figure should earn space by advancing the idea, evidence, prediction, comparison, or explanation.

stop_and_discuss.rule: Use Stop and Discuss when the preceding reading/representation benefits from verbal conceptual processing and that boundary is not already occupied by a canonical Example/YTI pair. Prompts are specific to the immediately preceding source content; no stock comprehension prompts.
stop_and_discuss.hewitt_source: Think and Discuss / Think and Explain / Think and Rank structures are preferred inspiration when they fit.

reading_apprenticeship.rule: Keep annotation, notice/wonder, evidence, model-reading, and representation interpretation opportunities purposeful; student workspaces may be generous for Notability.

student_teacher.student: clean Notability-first page with generous fixed workspace where required; use established keep-together wrappers and natural pagination
student_teacher.teacher: same instructional sequence, online-view-first, fixed student workspace heights released, answers/acceptable reasoning formatted as readable lists, teacher/student discourse moves as lists, and no overlap. Vertical space is not a concern.

teacher_support.multipart_solution_rule: Never render a multipart canonical solution as one long red paragraph. Break it into labeled/bulleted parts matching the student task.
preferred_order: Listen For / Likely Misconception when useful

pagination.rule: Use the established Notes/base CSS wrappers. Keep atomic instructional units together when practical. Do not wrap a giant multi-page reading in one avoid-break container.
pagination.forced_break_rule: Do not use forced page breaks for ordinary crowding/layout repair. Use them only for a genuinely intentional separate page/workspace required by the current Framework/shell.
